content.synthesis:
This audit illustrates a classic "institutional funding vs. PI-name discoverability" gap that frames how to interpret absence-of-evidence for senior PI-led leads in the U.S. solar-wind instrumentation community.

**Three-dimensional comparison.**
| Dimension | Stefano Livi (PI inside mission-line work) | Typical NSF PI Search Profile | Mission-line Instrument PI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Funding-record visibility | Lower: NASA/ESA contracts flow to SwRI, not under PI name | Higher: NSF Award Search indexes PIs | Moderate: institutional USASpending aggregate present, PI-level niche |
| Hiring-record visibility | Low -- UTSA-SwRI admissions page is the only program-level public channel; specific group openings are not always surfaced | Moderate -- postdoc ads on NSF/LinkedIn | Low -- mission work tends to fill via internal pipelines |
| Disambiguation risk | High (Italian namesake) -- multi-country LinkedIn/FB postings | Low (NSF drawfs namesake pool) | High (project-level PIs mixed across institutions) |

**Mechanism / implication.** The dimensionality of the overlook is consistent: PI-level grant search hits institutional aggregation layers; PI-level hiring search hits only official lab postings. The implication for this audit is that **a "no evidence found" finding for Livi on either dimension likely reflects the public discoverability architecture of senior instrument PIs, not necessarily a real absence** -- and so any user of this report should treat the funding and hiring blocks as "public indexes searched and currently silent for this name" rather than "funding/hiring not happening".

**Tension between findings.** The founding strength (five-source identity corroboration + two mission PI roles + a current grad student) is paired with a notable funding/hiring silence -- this tension arises because senior instrument PIs (a) generate mission-line work that is funded through institutional channels invisible to PI-search, and (b) recruit doctoral students through lab-student pipelines rather than job-post listings. The audit's confidence footprint is therefore asymmetric: highest on identity, lowest on externally visible funding/hiring in the 2024-2026 window.
